questions.question: In 1342, one of the nobles, Haji Ilyas Khan united Bengal and became its ruler under the title of ______and laid the foundation of the Ilyas Shah dynasty.
questions.solution:
In 1342, Shams-ud-din Ilyas Shah united the different regions of Bengal and founded the Ilyas Shah Dynasty.
  • He was the first independent ruler of unified Bengal.
  • He established his capital at Pandua.

questions.question: The war that spread beyond Southern India and into Bengal, where British forces under Robert Clive recaptured Calcutta from Nawab Sirajud-Daulah, who had the support of French, was ______.
questions.solution:
The Battle of Plassey (1757) saw Robert Clive recapture Calcutta and defeat Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah.
  • The Nawab was supported by a small French contingent.
  • The battle took place on the banks of the Bhagirathi River.

questions.question: The first President of the All India Trade Union Congress was _________.
questions.solution:
The first President of the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) was Lala Lajpat Rai in 1920.
  • AITUC was formed to provide Indian labor representation at the ILO.
  • Dewan Chaman Lall was its first General Secretary.

questions.question: Shivaji, the famous Maratha warrior fought against who among the following Mughal Emperors?
questions.solution:
The Maratha warrior Shivaji fought against the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.
  • Shivaji was imprisoned in Agra by Aurangzeb but famously escaped in a fruit basket.
  • The Treaty of Purandar (1665) was signed between Shivaji and Raja Jai Singh (on behalf of Aurangzeb).

questions.question: During The Battle of Chanderi or Siege of Chanderi, the Mughal Emperor ______ had defeated Rajputs in 1528.
questions.solution:
In the Battle of Chanderi (1528), Babur defeated the Rajput forces led by Medini Rai.
  • Chanderi was a strategic fort on the border of Malwa and Bundelkhand.
  • This victory further consolidated Babur's power in North India.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Bhoodan Yajna (Land Gift) movement?
questions.solution:
The Bhoodan Movement (Land Gift) was started by Vinoba Bhave in 1951.
  • The movement began in Pochampally village (now in Telangana).
  • It aimed to persuade wealthy landowners to voluntarily give land to landless farmers.

questions.question: With which of the following institutions is the name of Madan Mohan Malaviya associated?
questions.solution:
Madan Mohan Malaviya is primarily associated with the Banaras Hindu University.
  • He also played a key role in the Hindu Mahasabha.
  • He was given the title 'Mahamana' by Rabindranath Tagore.

questions.question: Who among the following Moroccan travellers came to India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
questions.solution:
The Moroccan traveler Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
  • He was appointed as a Qazi (judge) in Delhi.
  • He wrote the famous travelogue 'Rihla'.

questions.question: The Arya Samaj was founded in________ by Swami Dayanand Saraswati.
questions.solution:
The Arya Samaj was founded in 1875 by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in Bombay.
  • His motto was 'Go back to the Vedas'.
  • He wrote the book 'Satyarth Prakash'.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Viceroy of India during the formation of the Indian National Congress?
questions.solution:
Lord Dufferin was the Viceroy of India when the Indian National Congress was formed in 1885.
  • The first session was held in Bombay and presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee.
  • Dufferin initially called the INC a 'microscopic minority'.

questions.question: Malik Kafur was the commander of which among the following Khilji rulers, who sent him with his large army to conquer South India?
questions.solution:
Malik Kafur was the prominent general of Alauddin Khilji.
  • He led successful military campaigns into South India, reaching as far as Madurai.
  • He was originally a slave bought for 1,000 dinars (hence called 'Hazardinari').

questions.question: Who was the last sultan of the Lodi Dynasty?
questions.solution:
Ibrahim Lodi was the last sultan of the Lodi Dynasty and the Delhi Sultanate.
  • He was defeated and killed by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
  • He was the only Sultan of Delhi to die on the battlefield.

questions.question: ______ was a key position in the royal court of Delhi sultanate and his role was of a general supervisor over all departments.
questions.solution:
In the Delhi Sultanate, the Diwan-i-Wizarat was the department of the Wazir (Prime Minister).
  • He was the head of the revenue and finance department.
  • The Wazir exercised general supervision over all other departments.

questions.question: The ______ was a territorial assignment given to administrative officers and nobles in lieu of the services they performed for the state during Delhi sultanate.
questions.solution:
The Iqta system was a territorial assignment given to officers in lieu of cash salaries during the Delhi Sultanate.
  • The holders of these assignments were called Iqtadars or Muqtis.
  • The system was institutionalized by Iltutmish.
